title: SAARC, BIMSTEC and Regional Cooperation

cards.h: A region that trades with everyone but itself
cards.b:
South Asia holds about a quarter of humanity. Yet only around 5% of its trade is within the region, compared with over 20% in ASEAN. Border crossings are closed, flights are few and power grids barely connect.

This lesson asks why SAARC (1985) stalled, why India now prefers BIMSTEC and sub-regional deals, and what policy tools India uses: the Gujral Doctrine, Neighbourhood First, SAGAR and connectivity projects.

UPSC likes the comparison: SAARC versus BIMSTEC, and bilateralism versus regionalism. The theme links to functionalism and regional integration theory from Paper II Section A.

The founding members were Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka. Afghanistan became the eighth member in 2007. China, Japan, the US, the EU and others are observers.

The Charter (Article X) says decisions need unanimity and that bilateral and contentious issues are excluded. That rule was meant to protect smaller states from India, but it also stops the group from handling its main problem: India–Pakistan rivalry.

• India–Pakistan rivalry: after the Uri attack (September 2016), India and others pulled out of the Islamabad summit. No summit has happened since 2014.
  • Asymmetry: India is about 70% of the region's GDP and land. Neighbours fear dominance.
  • Pakistan's veto: the SAARC Motor Vehicles Agreement failed at Kathmandu in 2014 because Pakistan did not clear it. India then moved to BBIN (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Nepal), and the BBIN Motor Vehicles Agreement was signed in June 2015.
  • Low trade: SAFTA has many items on sensitive lists, and non-tariff barriers are high.
  • Trust: Pakistan denies India transit to Afghanistan. India denies Pakistan MFN trade status (withdrawn in 2019).

The South Asia Satellite (GSAT-9, 2017) was India's gift to the region, but Pakistan opted out.

The Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation began in Bangkok on 6 June 1997. Myanmar joined in December 1997, and Nepal and Bhutan in 2004. The Secretariat is in Dhaka.

It links South Asia and Southeast Asia and leaves Pakistan out. It was boosted by the BRICS–BIMSTEC outreach in Goa (October 2016) and Modi's invitation to leaders to his 2019 swearing-in.

  • Charter: adopted at the 5th summit in Colombo (30 March 2022).
  • 6th summit, Bangkok (April 2025): Modi attended. Bangladesh took the chair. A maritime transport cooperation agreement was signed.
  • Unfinished: the BIMSTEC FTA, begun in 2004, is still not concluded.

Gujral Doctrine (1996–97)

Five principles by I.K. Gujral: no reciprocity demanded from smaller neighbours; no territory used against another; no interference in internal affairs; respect for sovereignty; peaceful settlement of disputes.

Neighbourhood First (2014)

Modi invited all SAARC leaders to his 2014 swearing-in. Focus on connectivity, trade, lines of credit and quick delivery.

SAGAR (2015) and MAHASAGAR (2025)

Security and Growth for All in the Region, extended in 2025 to a wider 'mutual and holistic advancement' framework.

Other tools: the Colombo Security Conclave (India, Sri Lanka, Maldives, later Mauritius and Bangladesh), the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) and the Mekong–Ganga Cooperation.

cards.h: Integration theories applied to South Asia
cards.b:
Functionalism (David Mitrany, A Working Peace System, 1943)

Cooperate on technical tasks first. Habits of cooperation grow and make war less likely.

Neo-functionalism (Ernst Haas, The Uniting of Europe, 1958)

Cooperation in one sector 'spills over' into others.

Intergovernmentalism (Stanley Hoffmann)

States stay in charge and integrate only where their interests match.

South Asia fits intergovernmentalism best. Spillover has not happened because the core security rivalry blocks it. Karl Deutsch (Political Community and the North Atlantic Area, 1957) said integration needs a 'security community' where war is unthinkable. India and Pakistan are far from it.

Realists say regional integration cannot succeed while the two largest states are rivals. Functionalists reply that cooperation in low-politics areas such as power, transport and health can build habits of trust.

Sub-regionalism gives a middle path: BBIN, the Bhutan–India–Nepal power trade and the India–Bangladesh–Nepal energy deals (Nepal exports hydropower to Bangladesh via India, 2024). In 2025 reports described Chinese-backed talks among China, Pakistan and Bangladesh in Kunming on a possible alternative grouping, showing China's interest in the space.

• Treats SAARC as dormant and puts BIMSTEC at the centre of its Bay of Bengal policy.
  • Funds roads and rail: Kaladan, the Trilateral Highway, and India–Bangladesh rail links.
  • Offers Vaccine Maitri (2021) and disaster relief across the region, as in the 2015 Nepal earthquake and 2025 Myanmar earthquake relief (Operation Brahma).
  • Links payment systems: UPI in Nepal, Bhutan and Sri Lanka.

The tension: India is accused of acting alone while preaching consultation. Big projects still need local politics to line up.

SAARC

Founded 8 December 1985, Dhaka. 8 members. Secretariat: Kathmandu. Last summit: 2014.

BIMSTEC

Bangkok Declaration 1997. 7 members. Secretariat: Dhaka. Charter 2022. Latest summit: Bangkok, April 2025.

SAFTA

Signed 2004, in force 2006. Tariff phase-down for SAARC goods.

BBIN MVA

Signed 2015. Bhutan did not ratify, and the others proceeded on their own.

"SAARC has failed to achieve its objectives. Is BIMSTEC a better platform for India?" (typical)
"Examine India's Neighbourhood First policy." (typical)
"Discuss the challenges to regional cooperation in South Asia." (typical)

Structure: (1) SAARC's aims and record; (2) causes of failure: rivalry, asymmetry, unanimity; (3) BIMSTEC's strengths and gaps; (4) India's policy tools (Gujral, Neighbourhood First, SAGAR); (5) sub-regional initiatives (BBIN); (6) way forward: connectivity, trust, trade, working through functional areas.

quiz.w: India should give more than it asks of smaller neighbours.

quiz.w: June 2015 in Thimphu, after Pakistan blocked the SAARC version.
